question: What is the GIL in Python and how does it affect multithreading?

items.label: Q1
items.title: What is the GIL in Python?
items.text:
Question: What is the GIL in Python?
Source answer: The global interpreter lock lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time. CPU-bound threads therefore do not run in parallel, while I/O-bound threads still overlap their waiting because blocking I/O releases the lock.

goal: Explain the GIL's effect on threads

question: Design a chat application like WhatsApp; how are messages delivered when the receiver is offline?

items.label: Q8
items.title: Design a chat system
items.text:
Question: Design a chat system
Source answer: Clients keep a WebSocket to a chat server. Messages are written to a message store keyed by conversation; when the receiver is offline the message stays in an inbox queue and is pushed with a notification, then delivered when the device reconnects and acknowledges.

items.label: Q12
items.title: Explain the CAP theorem
items.text:
Question: Explain the CAP theorem
Source answer: During a network partition a distributed store must choose between consistency (every read sees the latest write or fails) and availability (every request gets a response). Without a partition both can be had.

items.label: Q13
items.title: Why does TCP use a three-way handshake?
items.text:
Question: Why does TCP use a three-way handshake?
Source answer: Both sides must learn and acknowledge each other's initial sequence number; two messages would leave the server unsure that the client received its sequence number, and stale duplicate SYNs could open a connection.

statement: two messages are not enough because the server needs confirmation of its sequence number

items.label: Q16
items.title: Design a rate limiter
items.text:
Question: Design a rate limiter
Source answer: Token bucket per API key in Redis: refill at rate r up to capacity B, take a token per request, reply 429 with Retry-After when empty. Sliding-window counters give stricter per-minute limits. Shard keys across Redis nodes; fail open or closed depending on the API.

question: What is the difference between git merge and git rebase?

items.label: Q27
items.title: git merge vs git rebase
items.text:
Question: git merge vs git rebase
Source answer: Merge joins histories with a merge commit and keeps them as they were; rebase replays your commits on top of the target branch, giving a linear history but rewriting commits, so avoid rebasing shared branches.
